title: Residual duality and numerical identities for subcanonical nodal clusters
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $X$ be a nonempty connected projective reduced $k$-scheme of pure dimension one [def-kun-projective, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-pure-dimension]. Assume $X$ is smooth except at ordinary nodes, meaning that at every singular closed point its completed local $k$-algebra is $k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Write $h^i(X,F)=\dim_kH^i(X,F)$ for Zariski module cohomology [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. Assume that for every decomposition $X=A\cup B$ into nonempty reduced unions of components with no common component, $\dim_k\Gamma(A\times_XB,\mathcal O_{A\times_XB})\ge2$ [def-weil-irreducible-components, def-pc-fibre-product]. Put $p_a(X)=1-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-euler-characteristic]. Let $S\subseteq X$ be a subcanonical zero-dimensional closed subscheme, with ideal $I_S$ and splitting index $r(S)$ in [def-sfb-subcanonical-splitting-index]. Write $F_S=I_S\otimes\omega_X$, $V_S=H^0(X,F_S)$, $\ell(S)=\dim_k\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)$ and $c(S)=2p_a(X)-\ell(S)-2\dim_kV_S$. Regard $V_S$ as a subspace of $H^0(X,\omega_X)$. For every $s\in V_S$ nonzero at every component generic point, evaluation at $s$ embeds $\mathcal Hom_X(F_S,\omega_X)$ into $\omega_X$; its image is $I_{S^*}\otimes\omega_X$ for a unique zero-dimensional closed subscheme $S^*\subseteq X$. This residual cluster is subcanonical, taking the residual twice with the same $s$ gives $S$, and
$$\ell(S)+\ell(S^*)=2p_a(X)-2,\qquad h^0(X,F_S)-h^0(X,F_{S^*})=p_a(X)-1-\ell(S),$$
$$c(S^*)=c(S).$$
All these section spaces are finite-dimensional. Moreover $h^0(X,\omega_X)=p_a(X)$ and $0\le\ell(S)\le2p_a(X)-2$. Here $\mathcal Hom$ is [def-pur-sheaf-hom], and tensor product is [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. No Cartier or reducedness condition on $S$ is imposed.

proof.text: Projectivity gives properness. Finite type over the Noetherian field gives a Noetherian curve. All coherent cohomology is finite-dimensional and vanishes above degree one. The global-functions lemma applies to this nonempty proper connected reduced curve and gives $h^0(\mathcal O_X)=1$. Hence, putting $g=h^1(\mathcal O_X)$, we have $p_a=1-(1-g)=g$. The nodal duality lemma supplies the invertible $\omega=\omega_X$ and $h^0(\omega)=g=p_a$. Its representing dualizing module agrees with the one for reduced curves by the uniqueness in that latter node, so $\chi(\omega)=-\chi(\mathcal O_X)=p_a-1$.

source.place: Tags 0BS2, 0BS3 and 0BS5; genus and global functions.

proof.text: The ideal description gives $I_S$ quasi-coherent. On this locally Noetherian scheme it is a coherent submodule of $\mathcal O_X$; tensoring with the locally trivial line $\omega$ gives a coherent submodule $F=I_S\omega\subseteq\omega$. The reduced-curve dualizing-module lemma says that a map to $\omega$ zero at all component generic points is zero; applied to a section map on an open (or its coherent image) this detects local sections of $F$. Apply the torsionfree-biduality lemma: $H=\mathcal Hom(F,\omega)$ is coherent, its local sections are detected generically, and $\delta_F$ is an isomorphism. At a component generic point $I_S=\mathcal O_X$ and the given $s$ is a basis of the one-dimensional $F_\eta=\omega_\eta$. Evaluation $\alpha:H\to\omega$, $\varphi\mapsto\varphi(s)$, is therefore an isomorphism at each such point. If a local section belongs to its kernel, all its generic germs vanish, so it is zero. Thus $\alpha$ is injective. Its coherent image $G$ has generic stalks $\omega_\eta$. In local bases of $\omega$, write $G=J\omega$; changing basis multiplies by a unit, so these ideals glue to a coherent ideal $J$. The affine quotients by $J$ glue to the unique closed subscheme $S^*$ with this ideal, and $G=I_{S^*}\omega$. Its support misses all component generic points, hence has dimension zero. The original inclusion $i:F\hookrightarrow\omega$ is a global section of $H$ and $\alpha(i)=s$. Consequently $s\in H^0(G)$ and $S^*$ is subcanonical.

source.place: Definition 2.10 and Remarks 2.11 and 2.13, printed pp.231–232; explicit bidual-evaluation argument. Local PDF WANTED; author-hosted primary text read online.

proof.text: Identify $H$ with $G$ by $\alpha$. The isomorphism $F\to\mathcal Hom(G,\omega)$ obtained from $\delta_F$ sends a local $f$ to the map $\alpha(\varphi)\mapsto\varphi(f)$. The section $s\in G$ is $\alpha(i)$, so evaluation of this map at $s$ is $i(f)$. Thus evaluation at the same $s$ on $\mathcal Hom(G,\omega)$ has image exactly $i(F)=I_S\omega$. The uniqueness of its ideal proves $(S^*)^*=S$ as closed subschemes, including their nilpotent structure.

source.place: Definition 2.10 and Remarks 2.11 and 2.13, printed pp.231–232; explicit bidual-evaluation argument. Local PDF WANTED; author-hosted primary text read online.

proof.text:
For either $T=S$ or $T=S^*$, the locally trivial line $\omega$ makes
$$0\longrightarrow I_T\omega\longrightarrow\omega\longrightarrow\omega/I_T\omega\longrightarrow0$$
exact. In local bases the quotient is $\mathcal O_X/I_T$ tensored with $\omega$. The zero-support Euler lemma gives $\chi(\omega/I_T\omega)=\chi(\mathcal O_X/I_T)=\dim_k\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)=\ell(T)$; the equality of section spaces here is precisely the quotient structure sheaf of the closed subscheme. Additivity therefore gives $\chi(F)=p_a-1-\ell(S)$ and $\chi(G)=p_a-1-\ell(S^*)$. The nodal Serre-duality isomorphism, valid for every coherent module, applied to $F$ gives $h^1(F)=h^0(H)=h^0(G)$. Applied to $G$ and using the actual isomorphism $\mathcal Hom(G,\omega)\cong F$ established in Step 3, it gives $h^1(G)=h^0(F)$. These dimensions are finite by Step 1. Thus $\chi(F)=h^0(F)-h^0(G)$ and $\chi(G)=-\chi(F)$.

source.place: Tag 0BS2 (5) applied to coherent ideals; varieties.tex Tag 0AYT (lemma-chi-tensor-finite), and Euler additivity.

proof.text:
Adding the two Euler identities from Step 4 gives $\ell(S)+\ell(S^*)=2p_a-2$, and the first gives $h^0(F)-h^0(G)=p_a-1-\ell(S)$. Substitute these two equalities into
$$c(S^*)-c(S)=\ell(S)-\ell(S^*)+2\bigl(h^0(F)-h^0(G)\bigr)$$
to obtain zero. Both lengths are dimensions of finite-dimensional vector spaces, hence nonnegative; the complementary-length identity gives $0\leq\ell(S)\leq2p_a-2$. Nothing in the argument used Cartierness or reducedness of either cluster. The two-connectedness hypothesis is stronger than needed for this residual-duality lemma.

The item statement is byte-identical to the one PASSed in Q46 08abe029: the r(S*)=r(S) clause stays dropped and two-connectedness is retained though unused, so nothing is weakened. The two added stmt_deps, the nodal-line node (ω_X) and the closed-immersion ideal-sheaf definition (I_S), are notions the statement uses. proof_deps equals the union of the step uses. Step 1: global-functions gives h^0(O)=1; the nodal ω agrees with the reduced-curve dualizing module by Yoneda and that node's uniqueness clause, so p_a=g, h^0(ω)=g and χ(ω)=p_a-1. Step 2: evaluation at s is injective because s_η is a basis of each generic stalk and the biduality node's detection clause applies. The image is Jω and V(J) is finite. α(i)=s, so S* is subcanonical. Step 3: under δ_F, ψ(s)=i(f), so (S*)*=S including nilpotent structure. Step 4: chi-zero-dim-support and Euler additivity give χ(F)=p_a-1-ℓ(S); Serre duality for every coherent sheaf plus Step 3 gives h^1(F)=h^0(G) and h^1(G)=h^0(F). Step 5: the substitution gives c(S*)=c(S) and 0≤ℓ≤2p_a-2. New node: Stacks dualizing.tex 0B5A (lemma-local-CM), the anti-equivalence of CM_d. It is true for torsion-free coherent modules on a reduced curve. I tested it on F=0, on ω, on m⊂k[[u,v]]/(uv) (dual is the normalization, double dual is m again) and on O_{C1} for a two-component curve. Searches over dag/nodes for bidual, reflexive, 0B5A, MCM and torsion-free with dualizing found no duplicate; it is generic and restates no clause of the item.
